definitions.gloss: to clench one's teeth; to grit one's teeth
definitions.explanation: To press the upper and lower teeth tightly together. Used both literally (physical clenching) and figuratively to describe enduring pain, hardship, or frustration with determination.

examples.japanese: {歯|は}を{食|く}いしばって{耐|た}えた。
examples.english: I gritted my teeth and endured it.

examples.japanese: {痛|いた}みに{歯|は}を{食|く}いしばりながら、ゴールまで{走|はし}り{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: Gritting my teeth against the pain, I kept running to the finish line.

examples.japanese: {悔|くや}しくて{涙|なみだ}が{出|で}そうだったが、{歯|は}を{食|く}いしばって{泣|な}かなかった。
examples.english: I was so frustrated I nearly cried, but I gritted my teeth and held back the tears.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used in the phrase {歯|は}を{食|く}いしばる. The figurative meaning of enduring hardship with determination is very common and carries a strong emotional tone of perseverance.

Godan verb (る → ら/り/る/れ/ろ): {食|く}いしばらない, {食|く}いしばります, {食|く}いしばる, {食|く}いしばれば, {食|く}いしばろう

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {歯|は}を{食|く}いしばる (to clench/grit one's teeth)
- {歯|は}を{食|く}いしばって{耐|た}える (to grit one's teeth and endure)
- {歯|は}を{食|く}いしばって{頑張|がんば}る (to grit one's teeth and persevere)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {食|く}いしばる: to clench teeth (endurance, determination)
- {噛|か}みしめる: to bite down on; to savor (can be physical or emotional)
- {我慢|がまん}する: to endure, to put up with (broader, no physical image)
